sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test imports
sections.what: Brings in the test tools and the catalog and mapping functions the tests check.

sections.name: sample
sections.title: Sample valid mapping input
sections.what: A complete, valid example of a mapping proposal that the tests modify to check each rule.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code; likely a single valid baseline so each test changes only one thing.
sections.watch_out: Because later tests copy this sample, a change to it can shift the results of many tests at once.

sections.name: source (part 1)
sections.title: Source and triage rule checks
sections.what: Defines a sample official-looking source and then checks the triage rules. The tests confirm the catalog counts, that public data hides partner and branding details, that generic phrases like national grid do not match a company, that Shell does not match inside seashell, that unconfirmed companies get no web domain, that missing values and timing are not scored high, that non-official sources cannot keep top confidence, that unquoted money and dates are removed, that old news stays provisional, and that a whitespace signal stays a hypothesis.
sections.why: The test names show the reasoning: avoid overstating value, urgency, and confidence, and avoid attaching news to the wrong company.
sections.watch_out: The first test checks exact catalog counts, so intentionally adding or removing catalog entries will fail it until the count is updated.

sections.name: source (part 2)
sections.title: Schema rejects bad tags and blocked offers
sections.what: Checks that the input schema accepts the sample, rejects an unknown trigger tag, and rejects a solution ID that is not allowed as the main offer.
sections.why: The schema is the first safety check on AI output, so these tests make sure it blocks unknown tags and blocked offers.
sections.watch_out: The blocked solution is identified by one specific ID; if the catalog reuses that ID, the test could pass for the wrong reason.

summary: Automated checks for the Opportunity Map triage rules: catalog counts, company name matching, scoring limits, withheld claims, legacy labelling, and input validation.
purpose: Stop changes from quietly weakening the rules that prevent overstated or wrongly attributed opportunities.
why: Reason not stated in the code as a whole; the test names show which rules they protect, such as not claiming high value without a quoted figure.
how: Uses a sample valid input and a sample official-looking source, then runs the finalising, legacy, account-matching and schema functions and asserts the expected results.
inputs: The sample input and source defined in the file, plus the catalog and mapping modules.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test, reported by Node's built-in test runner.
risks: Several tests depend on exact catalog counts, so every catalog change needs a matching update here. Passing tests do not prove the rules are complete.
debug: Run the file's tests and read the failing assertion. A failed count usually means catalog data changed on purpose; confirm the change before editing the expected number.
